description: The British Geological Survey runs the UK magnetic observatories at Lerwick, Eskdalemuir and Hartland and the World Data Centre for Geomagnetism in Edinburgh. Its data pages give UK observatory data (1-second and 1-minute means on application), historical magnetograms and yearbooks, magnetic indices, and global observatory annual means, survey data and historical observation records held by the WDC. The UK K-index series, listed on data.gov.uk, assigns a 0 to 9 activity code to each 3-hour interval for Lerwick, Eskdalemuir, Greenwich, Abinger and Hartland, hand scaled from 1954 to 1990 and automatically scaled since 1991. BGS also offers real-time services for the electricity supply industry (hourly standard deviation values from the three UK observatories as a GIC proxy for grid control rooms), alert and forecast services, and the BGS Global Geomagnetic Model under licence. Data are intended for academic use; BGS asks that they are not used commercially without contacting BGS Enquiries, and WDC data require acknowledgement of suppliers. Caveats: high-cadence observatory data are on application, not open download, and commercial users need an agreement. It supports geomagnetic storm inputs and validation for GIC models of the GB grid, pipelines and railway signalling; related records are the USGS geomagnetism observatories and the GFZ Kp index.
